meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have until twenty to five, Hale. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Start with who decided that, and when.
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Now the zero itself, Hale. On what basis?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
Turn the screen toward me, Hale. I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58. People write in one file and paste into another all the time, so what does that prove about where those words came from?
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.

I'm searching the scene now, Hale, and I'm writing down that line. A misquoted line is a mistake a tired seventeen-year-old can make, but whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

Thursday at 8:15, in your room, before any students arrive, and Owen does it to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Policy 4.4 says nothing goes in his record, and I want that from you in an email tonight, cc the principal. And the vice-principal keeps this to himself, Hale.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting today you agreed that Owen will do a supervised rewrite in your room on Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising, and that if it holds up the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I still require your written confirmation that nothing about this goes on Owen's record and that the rewrite stays private. I expect that confirmation in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite Thursday at 8:15, and she still wants written confirmation tonight, copied to the principal, that nothing goes on Owen's record and that it stays private.
What moved her: "That line is not in Hamlet." It was specific, tied to Owen's own essay, and she could check it herself.
What cost ground: nothing; you owned the gradebook mistake in one sentence and never relied on the detector or attacked Owen.
Try next time: when you offered the rewrite, put the no-record promise in writing on the spot and say who will know about it, because she was always going to demand both.
